# PCA, LAI, DATES, IBD

Here are a couple of ideas for smaller projects you could also work on to
practice simulations and modeling. Similarly to the case studies on [STRUCTURE
/ ADMIXTURE](project-structure.html) and [ADMIXTOOLS](project-admixtools.html),
they are all revolving around building models to generate ground-truth data for
use in:

1. benchmarking methods to decide which is the most appropriate for your
research problem,

2. validating the robustness of results from methods you already obtained,

3. developing simulation-based inference pipelines,

all using external software (rather than _slendr_-based statistics).

Unlike the many exercises in our tutorial sessions, I can't provide the
questions for you (let alone the answers). But, this is a workshop, and we can
definitely come up with ideas to tackle these together.











## PCA 

PCA is an incredibly popular method in population genetics, but there's been
quite a bit of controversy surrounding it, with a [highly
combative](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-022-14395-4) paper
criticizing the application of PCA in all of population genetics, almost to a
point of claiming that none of the published results can be really trusted.

As an example, take a look at [Figure
5](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-022-14395-4#Fig5) in the paper,
demonstrating that an Indian population can be arbitrarily placed in proximity
to Europeans, East Asians, and Africans, simply by tweaking the sample sizes of
all groups before they applying PCA on their genotype data.

If you're curious about this issue, you have now all the tools at your disposal
to be able to use _slendr_ to evaluate patterns and (un)expected behavior of
PCA in the light of the criticisms in the paper.

Things you could take a look into are:

- How do imbalanced sample sizes from different populations distort the shape
of a PCA compared to equal sample sizes?

- How does access to ancient DNA samples (or lack of ancient DNA samples) affect
the signal of admixture in a PCA? What other demographic factors could lead us to
false ideas about admixture in a PCA?

- Under which conditions does projection of ancient DNA samples on a PCA based
on modern DNA reference panel lead to misleading results?

- How is a phylogenetic tree structure in general reflected in a shape of PCA?

If you'd like an inspiration, you can take a look at a [work-in-progress
chapter about simulating PCA](popgen-nonspatial-pca.html) (but beware that it's
still unfinished and not proofread!). I suggest working with the convenient PCA
R package [_smartsnp_](https://christianhuber.github.io/smartsnp/).


## Local ancestry inference (LAI), DATES dating, and IBD segments

In the chapter on [simulating haplotypes](haplotype-methods.html) you've
learned about the _slendr_ functions `ts_tracts()` and `ts_ibd()`, which make
it possible to obtain perfect, exact, truth about admixture tracts and
haplotype sharing from customized simulations.

You've also learned how easy it is to generate VCF files from these
simulations. This opens up the possibility to generate genomic data from all
sorts of models relevant for your research questions and use them for all sorts
of applications briefly summarized in points 1.-3. at the beginning of this
chapter.

If you have software for LAI (such as MOSAIC, FLARE, RFMix, etc.), admixture
dating (DATES), or IBD inference (IBDSeq, IBIS, AncIBD), it's now very easy for
you to connect simulations with this kind of external software---the sky is the
limit!
